title: Pinch-pot mushroom cluster figurine in air-dry clay
subtitle: A group of three mushrooms built from pinched and modelled air-dry clay
excerpt: Three mushrooms of varying heights, each formed by pinching a dome cap and attaching a rolled stalk, clustered together on a shared clay base. No kiln is needed. The finished piece sits on a shelf or windowsill and can be painted in realistic or decorative colours.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. Pinch-building methods referenced from Encyclopedia Britannica 11th edition (1911) pottery entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: A clay form opened and shaped by pressing the thumb into a ball of clay and pinching the walls out
Clay diluted with water to a paste, used to join clay pieces together

content.text: Three mushrooms at different heights make a more interesting piece than one alone. Each cap is a small
pinch pot
dome pressed face-down; the stalk is a short coil pressed underneath. No kiln is required. The trio takes about 30 minutes to build and dries in 24 hours.
Building the mushroom caps
Pinch three balls of clay of different sizes: roughly 40 g, 25 g, and 15 g. These will become the three mushroom caps.

For each cap: press the thumb into the centre of the ball and pinch outward to form a bowl shape. Then invert the bowl face-down so the convex dome sits uppermost. This is the top of the mushroom cap.
Smooth the top of each dome with a damp sponge. If the rim of the inverted bowl looks raw, trim it with the needle tool to form a clean mushroom cap edge that curves inward slightly.
Building the stalks and base
Roll three cylinders of clay for stalks: 6 cm tall for the large mushroom, 4 cm for the medium, and 3 cm for the small. Each stalk should be about 12 mm in diameter.
Score the flat top of each stalk and the centre underside of each cap. Apply
slip
and press each cap firmly onto its stalk.

Roll a flat disc about 10 cm across and 8 mm thick for the shared base. Score the base of each assembled mushroom and score three spots on the disc. Apply slip and press the three mushrooms onto the disc in a cluster arrangement.
Drying and finishing
Allow to reach
bone-dry
over 24 to 48 hours. Apply two coats of PVA. Paint with acrylics: spotted red-and-white fly agaric colouring, earthy brown field mushroom tones, or a blue-green fantasy palette.
Variations
Use paper-clay for stronger stalks that are less likely to crack where they join the base. Add small moss textures to the base disc with a crumpled piece of foil pressed in before drying.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: Caps slide off the stalks during drying
items.cause: The joint was not scored and slipped on both surfaces
items.fix: Allow to dry; reattach with fresh slip on scored surfaces. Support the cap while the join firms up

items.cause: The stalk dried unevenly, with the base area drying faster than the middle
items.fix: Slow drying by covering with a loose cloth for the first 12 hours. Fill hairline cracks with slip at the leather-hard stage
